construct: Within the physiologic range, increased ventricular end-diastolic volume stretches cardiomyocyte sarcomeres and increases active force generation. The cellular Frank-Starling mechanism includes length-dependent activation with increased myofilament sensitivity to calcium, reduced lattice spacing, and titin/cross-bridge effects, allowing greater stroke volume at unchanged inotropic state.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: With heart rate, sympathetic drive, afterload, and calcium release held constant, increased filling raises stroke volume through intrinsic length-dependent activation of cardiac myofilaments.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Greater L-type calcium influx could increase force, but the stem fixes adrenergic state and calcium release; the response must therefore come from sarcomere-length-dependent myofilament properties.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: The isolated preload manipulation with unchanged calcium release uniquely supports increased myofilament calcium sensitivity at longer sarcomere length.
